item.title: Critiquing Dance and Movement
item.description: An imagined review of the contemporary dance piece The Narrow Room examines how the performers distribute weight, shape time, and move through space.

children.definition: Relating to the internally felt sense of bodily movement and position.
children.example: When the soloist presses her palms outward against empty space, the gesture has a kinesthetic effect: I can almost feel the resistance in my own shoulders.

children.definition: The passage of the body's load from one point of contact to another.
children.example: The opening step makes the weight transfer visible: her right foot takes her full weight before the left toes lift.
children.translation_uz: tana ogʻirligini bir tayanchdan boshqasiga oʻtkazish

children.definition: An arrangement in which opposing pulls or distributions of body weight offset each other and maintain equilibrium.
children.example: The duet finds a striking counterbalance when the partners clasp wrists and lean away from each other, keeping both sets of heels planted.
children.translation_ru: положение, в котором партнёры уравновешивают друг друга
children.translation_uz: sheriklar bir-birini muvozanatda ushlab turadigan holat

children.definition: Choreographed action predominantly performed with the body close to the ground.
children.example: The middle section commits to low-level movement: the dancers crawl on their forearms and slide on one hip, with their shoulders barely rising above their knees.
children.translation_ru: движение на нижнем уровне, близко к полу

children.definition: The clarity with which the actions of individual joints or body segments are differentiated within a gesture.
children.example: The articulation of the closing gesture is unusually clear: the elbow opens first, the wrist bends next, and the fingers unfold one by one.
children.translation_ru: чёткая работа отдельных суставов и частей тела
children.translation_uz: boʻgʻimlar va tana qismlari harakatining aniq ajratilishi

children.definition: The shaping of a movement sequence so that its flow and expressive quality continue across successive actions.
children.example: The soloist's sustained phrasing links a turn, a lunge and a rise into one continuous action, with the same measured intensity right through to the fingertips.
children.translation_uz: harakatlar ketma-ketligining ravonligi va ifodasini saqlagan holda ijro etish

children.definition: Rhythmic emphasis on a normally weak beat or subdivision within an established metre.
children.example: The trio's syncopation is clearest in the heel strikes: the dancers accent the second half of beat two and soften the landing on beat three.

children.definition: Performed with the body's main line deliberately tilted away from its usual vertical alignment over the base of support.
children.example: In the off-axis turn, the soloist keeps her torso pitched beyond the toes of her supporting foot and comes upright only as she steps out of the rotation.
children.translation_ru: выполняемый с наклоном оси тела относительно вертикали над опорой
children.translation_uz: tana oʻqi tayanch ustidagi tik holatdan ogʻgan holda bajariladigan

children.definition: A momentary impression that an upward or outward action is held at its fullest extent before the dancer yields to gravity.
children.example: A moment of suspension at the top of the rise makes the soloist seem to hover on the balls of her feet before her heels sink.
children.translation_ru: эффект зависания в верхней точке движения

children.definition: The performance of the same movement by two or more dancers at the same time.
children.example: The quartet folds in unison, with every knee bending and every chin dropping at exactly the same instant.
children.translation_uz: ayni harakatning bir vaqtda ijro etilishi

children.definition: A choreographic structure in which dancers begin the same movement sequence at staggered times.
children.example: The canon travels down the line as each dancer begins the same three-gesture sequence one beat after the person beside them.

children.definition: The line traced through space by a dancer or a moving body part.
children.example: The lead dancer's trajectory forms a broad arc across the rear of the stage before curling inward toward the centre.

children.definition: A deliberate absence of visible motion used as part of a performance.
children.example: The quartet maintains complete stillness after the last heel strike, with hands at their sides and gazes fixed until the stage goes dark.

children.definition: Muscular tightness that can be seen or felt in a dancer’s posture or movement.
children.example: The tension in the soloist's forearms remains visible even as her wrists circle freely, giving the gesture a tightly controlled quality.
